subproblem.title: Smooth cutoff: χ = 1 near a compact K, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, compact support inside an open U
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and K ⊆ U compact (ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). Then there are a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) and an open set N ⊆ ℝ^P such that 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for every x, χ has compact support (HasCompactSupport χ), tsupport χ ⊆ U, K ⊆ N and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ (χ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) ∧ HasCompactSupport χ ∧ tsupport χ ⊆ U ∧ IsOpen N ∧ K ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, χ x = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (Cutoff) of the parent proof of fiw_tb_extend_to_univ, written out for ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). This is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence locally compact and Hausdorff, so its compact subsets are closed.

1. (Two compact neighbourhoods.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U. By local compactness there is a compact set L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ U (Mathlib exists_compact_between). Apply the same fact to K and the open set interior L (isOpen_interior; K ⊆ interior L). This gives a compact set L₁ with K ⊆ interior L₁ and L₁ ⊆ interior L.
2. (Smooth Urysohn function.) L₁ is compact, hence closed; interior L is open; and L₁ ⊆ interior L. The smooth Urysohn lemma for finite-dimensional real normed spaces (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with smoothness n := (⊤ : ℕ∞), s := interior L, t := L₁) gives f : ℝ^P → ℝ with:
   - ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f;
   - range f ⊆ [0, 1];
   - support f = interior L;
   - for every x, x ∈ L₁ ⟺ f(x) = 1.
   (Alternatively, use exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), s := K, t := L, then contMDiff_iff_contDiff. The argument below only needs the listed properties.)
3. Put χ := f and N := interior L₁.
   (a) χ is C^∞ by step 2.
   (b) For every x, χ(x) ∈ range f ⊆ [0, 1], i.e. 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1.
   (c) support χ = interior L ⊆ L, and L is closed. So tsupport χ = closure(support χ) ⊆ L (closure_minimal), hence tsupport χ ⊆ L ⊆ U.
   (d) tsupport χ is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and contained in the compact set L, so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). That is, HasCompactSupport χ.
   (e) N = interior L₁ is open (isOpen_interior), and K ⊆ N by step 1.
   (f) If x ∈ N then x ∈ L₁ (interior_subset), so χ(x) = 1 by step 2.
4. Properties (a)–(f) are exactly the assertions of the lemma. ∎

  intro P U K hU hK hKU
  obtain ⟨L, hL, hKL, hLU⟩ := exists_compact_between hK hU hKU
  obtain ⟨L₁, hL₁, hKL₁, hL₁L⟩ := exists_compact_between hK isOpen_interior hKL
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfr, hfs, hf1⟩ :=
    exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (n := (⊤ : ℕ∞)) isOpen_interior hL₁.isClosed hL₁L
  have htsupp : tsupport f ⊆ L :=
    closure_minimal (hfs.symm ▸ interior_subset) hL.isClosed
  refine ⟨f, interior L₁, hf, fun x => hfr (mem_range_self x), ?_, htsupp.trans hLU,
    isOpen_interior, hKL₁, fun x hx => (hf1 x).mp (interior_subset hx)⟩
  exact hL.of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_tsupport _) htsupp
proof_key_steps: exists_compact_between twice: compact L, L₁ with K ⊆ interior L₁ ⊆ L₁ ⊆ interior L ⊆ L ⊆ U.
Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff): f is C^∞ with values in [0, 1], support f = interior L, and f = 1 exactly on L₁.
tsupport f ⊆ L because L is closed; hence f has compact support contained in U.
N := interior L₁ is open, contains K, and f = 1 on N.

subproblem.title: A current vanishing off K only sees test forms on a neighbourhood of K
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ and V, K, N ⊆ ℝ^P with N open and K ⊆ N. Let Z ∈ D_q(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V q) satisfy Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) (TestFormOn V q) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Then Z(η) = Z(ω) for all ω, η ∈ D^q(V) with η(x) = ω(x) for every x ∈ N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K N : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen N → K ⊆ N → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → ∀ ω η : TestFormOn V q, (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) → Z η = Z ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (vanishing fact (V)) of the parent proof, in the form used in steps 5, 8 and (B5). There η = χ•ω with χ = 1 on N, so η and ω agree on N. The hypothesis "Z vanishes on test forms supported off K" replaces the parent's appeal to spt Z ⊆ K and vanish_off_support; the parent derives this hypothesis from spt Z ⊆ K.

1. Put ζ := η − ω ∈ D^q(V). D^q(V) is a real vector space with pointwise operations, so ζ(x) = η(x) − ω(x). For x ∈ N, ζ(x) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence support ζ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N.
2. N is open, so ℝ^P ∖ N is closed. Therefore tsupport ζ = closure(support ζ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N (closure_minimal).
3. K ⊆ N, so ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K. By step 2, tsupport ζ is disjoint from K.
4. By the hypothesis on Z, Z(ζ) = 0. Z is linear (Z.toCurrent is a linear map; map_sub), so Z(ζ) = Z(η) − Z(ω). Hence Z(η) = Z(ω). ∎

Reference Lean proof (kernel-checked in a scratch build importing GMT.Ch06.Submission, in the comparator's contract scope; sibling dependencies are referenced as Submission.X):
theorem Submission.fiw_tb_ext_apply_eq_of_eqOn : ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K N : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen N → K ⊆ N → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → ∀ ω η : TestFormOn V q, (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) → Z η = Z ω := by
  intro P q V K N Z hN hKN hZ ω η hηω
  have hsupp : tsupport ((η - ω : TestFormOn V q) : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) ⊆ Nᶜ := by
    apply closure_minimal _ hN.isClosed_compl
    intro x hx hxN
    apply hx
    change (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = 0
    rw [hηω x hxN, sub_self]
  have h0 : Z (η - ω) = 0 :=
    hZ _ (Disjoint.mono_left hsupp (disjoint_compl_left.mono_right hKN))
  have h1 : Z (η - ω) = Z η - Z ω := Z.toCurrent.map_sub η ω
  rw [h1] at h0
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp h0
proof_key_steps: ζ := η − ω vanishes on the open set N, so tsupport ζ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N.
ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K ⊆ N, so Z(ζ) = 0 by hypothesis.
Linearity: Z(η) − Z(ω) = Z(ζ) = 0.

audit.reason: The difference η−ω vanishes on open N, so its topological support lies in the closed complement, disjoint from K. The vanishing hypothesis and linearity give exactly Z η = Z ω.

subproblem.title: Homogeneity of the Euclidean coefficient norm: |cα| = |c|·|α|
subproblem.statement: For all P, q ∈ ℕ, every c ∈ ℝ and every q-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) q: covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| · covectorEuclideanNorm α. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin P} t_I(α)), where t_I(α) = α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)})² if I is strictly increasing and t_I(α) = 0 otherwise, and e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (c : ℝ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) q), covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the homogeneity fact |tα| = |t|·|α| stated in the Notation paragraph and used in step 4(a) of the parent proof. It is also step 1 of the accepted proof of br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass.

1. Scalar multiplication of continuous alternating maps is pointwise (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). So for every I : Fin q → Fin P, (c • α)(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}) = c·α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}).
   - For strictly increasing I: t_I(c • α) = (c·α(e_I))² = c²·t_I(α) (mul_pow).
   - For the other I: t_I(c • α) = 0 = c²·t_I(α).
2. Summing over the finitely many I gives Σ_I t_I(c • α) = c²·s, where s := Σ_I t_I(α) ≥ 0 (Finset.mul_sum).
3. Therefore:
   covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = √(c²·s)
   = √(c²)·√s (Real.sqrt_mul, as c² ≥ 0)
   = |c|·√s (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs)
   = |c|·covectorEuclideanNorm α. ∎

Reference Lean proof (kernel-checked in a scratch build importing GMT.Ch06.Submission, in the comparator's contract scope; sibling dependencies are referenced as Submission.X):
theorem Submission.fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul : ∀ (P q : ℕ) (c : ℝ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) q), covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| * covectorEuclideanNorm α := by
  intro P q c α
  unfold covectorEuclideanNorm
  rw [← Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, ← Real.sqrt_mul (sq_nonneg c), Finset.mul_sum]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun I _ => ?_
  split_ifs
  · simp only [ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_pow]
  · simp
proof_key_steps: (c•α)(e_I) = c·α(e_I), so each squared coefficient is multiplied by c².
Factor c² out of the finite sum.

audit.reason: Pointwise scalar multiplication multiplies every squared coefficient by c², including the zero summands. Factoring the finite sum and applying the square-root identities proves the exact equality for all P, q and c.

subproblem.title: Multiplying test forms by a smooth function supported in W is a linear map D^q(V) → D^q(W)
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let V, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, and let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) with tsupport χ ⊆ W. Then there is an ℝ-linear map L : D^q(V) → D^q(W) (TestFormOn V q →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn W q) such that (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every ω ∈ D^q(V) and every x ∈ ℝ^P. This is an identity of underlying forms; χ(x)·ω(x) is the scalar multiple of the covector ω(x).

- HasCompactSupport φ;
- tsupport φ ⊆ W.

1. Fix ω ∈ D^q(V) and put φ_ω(x) := χ(x)·ω(x).
   (a) Smoothness. χ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞, and ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) q is C^∞ since ω ∈ D^q(V). So the pointwise scalar product φ_ω is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
   (b) Compact support.
       - tsupport φ_ω ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_smul_subset_right), and tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport ω).
       - tsupport φ_ω is closed (isClosed_tsupport), so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport φ_ω.

   (c) Support in W. tsupport φ_ω ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ W, by tsupport_smul_subset_left and the hypothesis.
   Hence φ_ω ∈ TestFormOn W q.
2. Define L(ω) := ⟨φ_ω, step 1⟩ ∈ D^q(W). By construction (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for all x.

   (b) for c ∈ ℝ, L(cω)(x) = χ(x)·(c·ω(x)) = c·(χ(x)·ω(x)) = (c·Lω)(x) (smul_comm).
   So L, with map_add' from (a) and map_smul' from (b), is a linear map TestFormOn V q →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn W q.
4. L satisfies the asserted pointwise formula (step 2). ∎

subproblem.title: A current vanishing on test forms supported off a closed set K has support in K
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ ℝ^P closed, and Z ∈ D_q(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Then spt Z ⊆ K. Here spt Z = Z.support = V ∖ zeroRegion(Z), and zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ V and Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen V → IsClosed K → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → Z.support ⊆ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 (spt Y ⊆ K, with V = ℝ^P) and (B1) (spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K, with V = U) of the parent proof, in one common form. Recall that Z.VanishesOn W means Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

1. Let x ∈ spt Z, so x ∈ V and x ∉ zeroRegion(Z). Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ K.
2. V ∖ K is open (V open, K closed; IsOpen.sdiff) and contains x. So there is ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ V ∖ K (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r := ε/2 > 0 and W := ball(x, r).
3. Properties of W.
   - W is open.
   - closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). closedBall(x, r) is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall), and closure W is closed, so closure W is compact.
   - closedBall(x, r) ⊆ ball(x, ε) since r < ε (closedBall_subset_ball). Hence closure W ⊆ ball(x, ε) ⊆ V ∖ K ⊆ V.
4. Z.VanishesOn W. Let ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since W ⊆ ball(x, ε) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ K, tsupport ω is disjoint from K, so Z(ω) = 0 by hypothesis.
5. By steps 3–4, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion(Z), and x ∈ W because r > 0. So x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting step 1. Hence x ∈ K, and spt Z ⊆ K. ∎

  by_contra hxK
  obtain ⟨hxV, hxz⟩ := hx
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp (hV.sdiff hK) x ⟨hxV, hxK⟩
  apply hxz
  refine ⟨ball x (ε / 2), ⟨isOpen_ball, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, mem_ball_self (half_pos hε)⟩
  · exact (isCompact_closedBall x (ε / 2)).of_isClosed_subset isClosed_closure
      closure_ball_subset_closedBall
  · exact (closure_ball_subset_closedBall.trans
      (closedBall_subset_ball (half_lt_self hε))).trans (hball.trans sdiff_subset)
  · intro ω hω
    apply hZ
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro y hy hyK
    exact (hball (ball_subset_ball (half_le_self hε.le) (hω hy))).2 hyK

subproblem.title: If M(X) < ∞, then ω ↦ X(χω) is a current on ℝ^P
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. Let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) with tsupport χ ⊆ U and |χ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let X ∈ D_q(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U q) have finite mass, M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ≠ ∞. Then there is Y ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q: a linear functional on D^q(ℝ^P) that is sequentially continuous at 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges) such that Y(ω) = X(η) for all ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) and η ∈ D^q(U) with η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (χ : Eucl P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ → tsupport χ ⊆ U → (∀ x, |χ x| ≤ 1) → ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U q, X.mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q) (η : TestFormOn U q), (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) → Y ω = X η
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof: the definition Y(ω) := X(χω) and its sequential continuity via the finite mass of X.
- The parent's sub-steps 4(b)–(c) (coefficient norm versus operator norm, and uniform smallness of a null sequence) are exactly the reused sibling converges_small.
- Sub-step 4(a) is the reused sibling eval_bound.

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. μ_X := (X.mass).toReal, a real number ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_nonneg), finite because M(X) ≠ ∞.

1. (Multiplication map.) Apply the sibling smul_testform (Submission.fiw_tb_ext_smul_testForm) with V := ℝ^P (univ), W := U and χ (C^∞, tsupport χ ⊆ U). It gives a linear map L : D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U) with (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for all ω and x.
2. (The functional.) Let Y₀ := X ∘ L, i.e. Y₀(ω) = X(Lω). It is linear as a composition of linear maps (X.toCurrent.comp L).
3. (Sequential continuity.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in D^q(ℝ^P) with TestFormOnConverges ω 0. We show Y₀(ω_j) → 0.
   (a) By the reused sibling converges_small (Submission.fiw_ims_sc_converges_zero_small) with U := ℝ^P: for every δ > 0 there is j₀ such that |ω_j(x)| ≤ δ for all j ≥ j₀ and all x ∈ ℝ^P (eventually_atTop).
   (b) For such j and every x, the sibling norm_smul and |χ(x)| ≤ 1 give |(Lω_j)(x)| = |χ(x)·ω_j(x)| = |χ(x)|·|ω_j(x)| ≤ 1·δ = δ.
   (c) Let ε > 0 and take δ := ε/(μ_X + 1) > 0 in (a). Let j ≥ j₀. Apply the reused sibling eval_bound (Submission.br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass) to X ∈ D_q(U), the test form Lω_j ∈ D^q(U), C := δ > 0 (admissible by (b)) and M(X) ≠ ∞. It gives |Y₀(ω_j)| = |X(Lω_j)| ≤ δ·μ_X.
   (d) δ·μ_X = ε·μ_X/(μ_X + 1) < ε, since ε·μ_X < ε·(μ_X + 1) for ε > 0. Hence |Y₀(ω_j) − 0| < ε for all j ≥ j₀. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, Y₀(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_atTop).
   So Y := ⟨Y₀, step 3⟩ is an element of GeometricCurrentOn univ q; its continuity field is exactly the statement of step 3.
4. (Characterization.) Let ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) and η ∈ D^q(U) with η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every x. Then (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) = η(x) for every x. So Lω = η in D^q(U) (Subtype.ext, funext), and Y(ω) = X(Lω) = X(η). ∎

  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := Submission.fiw_tb_ext_smul_testForm P q (univ : Set (Eucl P)) U χ hχ hχU
  refine ⟨⟨X.toCurrent.comp L, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro ωs hωs
    obtain ⟨K, -, -, -, hsmall⟩ := Submission.fiw_ims_sc_converges_zero_small P q univ ωs hωs
    rw [Metric.tendsto_atTop]
    intro ε hε
    set μX := X.mass.toReal with hμX
    have hμ0 : 0 ≤ μX := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    have hδ : 0 < ε / (μX + 1) := by positivity
    obtain ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (hsmall (ε / (μX + 1)) hδ)
    refine ⟨j₀, fun j hj => ?_⟩
    rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero]
    have hbound : ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm
        ((L (ωs j) : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) ≤ ε / (μX + 1) := by
      intro x
      rw [hL, Submission.fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul]
      calc |χ x| * covectorEuclideanNorm ((ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x)
          ≤ 1 * (ε / (μX + 1)) :=
            mul_le_mul (hχ1 x) (hj₀ j hj x) (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg _) zero_le_one
        _ = ε / (μX + 1) := one_mul _
    have hX' := Submission.br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass P q U X (L (ωs j)) (ε / (μX + 1)) hδ hbound hX
    change |X (L (ωs j))| < ε
    calc |X (L (ωs j))| ≤ ε / (μX + 1) * μX := hX'
      _ < ε := by
        rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
        nlinarith
  · intro ω η hη
    change X (L ω) = X η
    congr 1
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext x
    rw [hL, hη]
proof_key_steps: L := multiplication by χ, a linear map D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U) (sibling smul_testform); Y₀ := X ∘ L.
For ω_j → 0: converges_small gives sup_x |ω_j(x)| ≤ δ eventually, and norm_smul with |χ| ≤ 1 gives sup_x |(Lω_j)(x)| ≤ δ.
eval_bound: |X(Lω_j)| ≤ δ·M(X); with δ = ε/(M(X) + 1) this is < ε, so Y₀(ω_j) → 0.
Y := ⟨X ∘ L, continuity⟩. Lω = η whenever η = χω pointwise, so Y(ω) = X(η).

Uniform coefficient smallness, scalar homogeneity and the finite-mass evaluation bound prove sequential continuity using δ=ε/(X.mass.toReal+1). Pointwise equality identifies every eligible η with Lω. subproblem.title: Lemma B: if Z on ℝ^P vanishes off a compact K ⊆ U and Z|_U is integer multiplicity, then so is Z
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, and Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Suppose Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) is an integer multiplicity current in U. That is, Z|_U = τ(M, θ, ξ) on D^q(U) for a rectifiable triple with IsRectifiableTriple U q M θ ξ and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M. Then Z is an integer multiplicity current in ℝ^P (IsIntegerMultiplicity Z, with a triple relative to univ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z

Source: step 9 (Lemma B, (B1)–(B5)) of the parent proof.
- In (B2), the support-null fact H^q(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0 comes from the reused sibling rect_support_null (Submission.lpf_rectifiable_support_null). It has the same conclusion as the parent's sibling support_null, but no MF hypothesis.
- In (B3)–(B4), the blow-up/tangent congruence is the reused sibling tangent_congr (Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr). As the parent's Remark indicates, the special case used is V := ℝ^P, M' := M ∩ K, θ' := θ.

Notation.
- H := H^q = μHE[q], and H⌞A := H.restrict A.
- τ(M, θ, ξ)(φ) := tauAction q M θ ξ φ = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)) dH(x).
- ι := testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q; it does not change the underlying form.

1. (Data.) By hypothesis there are M, θ, ξ with:
   - IsRectifiableTriple U q M θ ξ;
   - θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M;
   - Z|_U(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^q(U).
2. ((B1): spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K.) Let ω ∈ D^q(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from K. Then Z|_U(ω) = Z(ιω) = 0 by the hypothesis on Z, since ιω has the same underlying form and hence the same tsupport. U is open, and K is closed (compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P). So the sibling support_subset with V := U gives spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K.
3. ((B2): H(M ∖ K) = 0.) The reused sibling rect_support_null, applied to T := Z|_U and the triple of step 1, gives H(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0. By step 2, M ∖ K ⊆ M ∖ spt(Z|_U), so H(M ∖ K) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
4. Put M' := M ∩ K.
   - M' ∖ M = ∅, and M ∖ M' = M ∖ K is H-null. So M' and M are H-a.e. equal (ae_eq_set), and H⌞M' = H⌞M (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
   - symmDiff M M' = (M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∖ M) ⊆ M ∖ K, hence H(symmDiff M M' ∩ ℝ^P) = 0.
5. ((B3)–(B4): (M', θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P.) We verify the seven fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ q M' θ ξ.
   (a) subset: M' ⊆ ℝ^P = univ.
   (b) nullMeasurableSet: M is H-null-measurable and K is closed, hence measurable. So M' = M ∩ K is H-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter).
   (c) countablyRectifiable: M' ⊆ M, and M is countably q-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   (d) pos: θ > 0 on M ⊇ M'.
   (e) integrableOn: let K'' ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K, because K is a compact subset of U (field integrableOn of the U-triple). Since M' ∩ K'' ⊆ M ∩ K, θ is H-integrable on M' ∩ K'' (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
   (f) aestronglyMeasurable: ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M = H⌞M' (step 4).
   (g) orients: since H⌞M' = H⌞M, it suffices to show the following for H⌞M-a.e. x: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin q → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M' θ x (span(range τ)) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
       - The U-triple gives, for H⌞M-a.e. x, an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M θ x (span(range τ)) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
       - For such x, apply the reused sibling tangent_congr with (M, M', θ, θ', x, V) := (M, M', θ, θ, x, ℝ^P). Its hypotheses hold: ℝ^P is open and contains x; H(symmDiff M M' ∩ ℝ^P) = 0 by step 4; θ = θ everywhere; θ(x) = θ(x).
       - It gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M' θ x (span(range τ)), so the same τ works (filter_upwards).
6. (Integrality.) For x ∈ M' ⊆ M, θ(x) ∈ ℕ by step 1.
7. ((B5): representation.)
   - The sibling cutoff gives a C^∞ χ with tsupport χ ⊆ U and an open N ⊇ K with χ = 1 on N.
   - The sibling smul_testform (V := ℝ^P, W := U) gives a linear L : D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U) with (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x).
   Let ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P).
   (a) ι(Lω) and ω agree on N, because χ = 1 there. So the sibling eq_near (V := ℝ^P, with the vanishing hypothesis on Z) gives Z(ω) = Z(ι(Lω)) = Z|_U(Lω).
   (b) By step 1 and H⌞M = H⌞M' (step 4): Z|_U(Lω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH(x) = ∫_{M'} θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH(x).
   (c) For x ∈ M' we have x ∈ K ⊆ N, so χ(x) = 1 and θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)). M' is H-null-measurable (5(b)), so setIntegral_congr_fun₀ gives ∫_{M'} θ·ξ(χω) dH = ∫_{M'} θ·ξ(ω) dH = τ(M', θ, ξ)(ω).
   Hence Z(ω) = τ(M', θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P).
8. By steps 5, 6 and 7, (M', θ, ξ) witnesses IsIntegerMultiplicity Z. ∎

subproblem.title: Lemma A: a current on ℝ^P vanishing off a compact K ⊆ U has M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U)
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, and Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Let Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) ∈ D_q(U), so Z|_U(ω) = Z(ω) for ω ∈ D^q(U) ⊆ D^q(ℝ^P). Then M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U), where M(Z) = Z.mass = Z.massOn univ and M(Z|_U) = (Z|_U).mass = (Z|_U).massOn U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → Z.mass ≤ (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 (Lemma A) of the parent proof. The vanishing fact (V) is the sibling eq_near, applied with the hypothesis that Z vanishes on test forms supported off K. (The parent obtains this hypothesis from spt Z ⊆ K.)

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. ι := testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q : D^q(U) → D^q(ℝ^P); it does not change the underlying form.

1. (Cutoff.) Apply the sibling cutoff (Submission.fiw_tb_ext_cutoff) to U open and K ⊆ U compact. It gives a C^∞ χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and tsupport χ ⊆ U, and an open N ⊇ K with χ = 1 on N.
2. (Multiplication.) The sibling smul_testform with V := ℝ^P, W := U gives a linear L : D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U) with (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x).
3. (Reduction.) By definition, M(Z) = Z.massOn univ is the supremum of ofReal(Z(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ q univ. These are the ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to show ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ M(Z|_U) for each such ω (sSup_le).
4. (Admissibility.) Fix such an ω. Then Lω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U q U:
   - tsupport(Lω) ⊆ U, because Lω ∈ D^q(U);
   - for every x, the sibling norm_smul and 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 give |(Lω)(x)| = |χ(x)|·|ω(x)| = χ(x)·|ω(x)| ≤ 1·1 = 1.
5. (Locality.) For x ∈ N, (ι(Lω))(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) = ω(x), because χ(x) = 1. Apply the sibling eq_near with V := ℝ^P, the sets K ⊆ N (N open) and the vanishing hypothesis on Z. It gives Z(ι(Lω)) = Z(ω).
6. Hence Z(ω) = Z(ι(Lω)) = Z|_U(Lω) (GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply). By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn and step 4, ofReal(Z(ω)) = ofReal(Z|_U(Lω)) ≤ (Z|_U).massOn U = M(Z|_U).
7. Taking the supremum over all ω in step 3 gives M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U). ∎

  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := Submission.fiw_tb_ext_smul_testForm P q (univ : Set (Eucl P)) U χ hχs hχU
  apply sSup_le
  rintro r ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩
  have hadm : L ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U q U := by

    rw [hL, Submission.fiw_tb_ext_covectorNorm_smul, abs_of_nonneg (hχ01 x).1]
    calc χ x * covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) ≤ 1 * 1 :=

    rw [GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply]
    symm
    apply Submission.fiw_tb_ext_apply_eq_of_eqOn P q univ K N Z hN hKN hZ ω
      (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q (L ω))
    intro x hx
    change (L ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = _
    rw [hL, hχN x hx, one_smul]

  rw [hval]
  exact (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).le_massOn hadm
